subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 34-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of fatigue, easy bruising, and gingival bleeding. Laboratory studies show pancytopenia, a prolonged prothrombin time, and elevated D-dimer. Peripheral blood smear reveals many abnormal promyelocytes containing multiple Auer rods, and cytogenetic testing demonstrates t(15;17). He is started on a differentiating agent together with arsenic trioxide and achieves remission.
question: Which of the following agents most directly induces terminal differentiation of these malignant cells?
explanation_correct: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is driven by the t(15;17) PML-RARA fusion, which blocks retinoic acid receptor signaling and arrests myeloid maturation. All-trans retinoic acid overcomes this block and drives terminal differentiation of the leukemic promyelocytes, rapidly improving the coagulopathy; it is combined with arsenic trioxide.

explanation_incorrect.A: Cytarabine is an antimetabolite that kills dividing cells by incorporating into DNA; it does not induce differentiation of promyelocytes.
explanation_incorrect.B: Imatinib inhibits the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase of chronic myeloid leukemia and is not active in acute promyelocytic leukemia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and is used in other hematologic and rheumatic diseases; it does not differentiate promyelocytes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 antibody used for B-cell lymphomas and has no role in a myeloid leukemia whose cells lack CD20.

educationalObjective: All-trans retinoic acid treats t(15;17) acute promyelocytic leukemia by overcoming the PML-RARA maturation block and inducing terminal differentiation of promyelocytes.
